title: Incidents in Agentic SOC: the Incidents page, detail tabs, verdicts, statuses, custom incidents and customization

checks.do: Which verdict and status values an analyst can set: the Taking Action on Incidents page lists them; the Create Incident from Alerts drawer gives different examples.

page-columns.statement: The Incidents page table displays columns by default, including ID, Severity, Type, Title, Created, Alerts Count, Sources, Assignee, Status and Verdict.

quotes: The table displays the following columns by default:
ID: The ID number of the incident.
Severity: The severity of the incident (e.g., Critical, High, Medium).
Type: The type of incident (e.g., AI, Platform, Custom).
Title: The title of the incident.
Created: The date the incident was created.
Alerts Count: The number of alerts associated with the incident.
Sources: The sources of the threat data
Assignee: The user assigned to the incident.
Status: The status of the incident (e.g., Discovered, Confirmed, Closed).
Verdict: The verdict for the incident (e.g., Malicious, Suspicious, Benign).

page-actions.statement: From the Incidents page you can modify multiple incidents at once (for example updating the status, merging incidents and adding comments), save a view, export the table to a CSV file, and see the number of incidents by status, severity and verdict as charts.

quotes: Modify multiple incidents at once, such as updating the status, merging incidents together, and adding comments.
Save your view for quick access after making adjustments to it
export table data to a CSV file
See the number of incidents by status, severity, and verdict, displayed as charts.

detail-tabs.statement: An incident's detail page has tabs Details, Affected Entities, Timeline, Attack Path (events overlaid on the MITRE ATT&CK matrix), Analysis (leads explored by the Investigation Agent), Alerts (the alerts and sources the Enrichment and Correlation Agents used to create the incident), Activity (an audit log) and Comments.

quotes: Details: Summarizes the activity included in the incident
Affected Entities: Lists the assets and users involved in the incident.
Timeline: Displays the chronological order of events included in the incident.
Attack Path: Overlays events on the MITRE ATT&CK matrix
Analysis: Summarizes the investigative leads explored by the Investigation Agent.
Alerts: Shows which alerts and sources Agentic SOC's Enrichment and Correlation Agents used to create the incident.
Activity: Shows an audit log of all activities related to the incident
Comments: Shows all comments added by analysts.

verdicts.statement: The Taking Action on Incidents page lists six verdicts that analysts and agents can set: Benign, False Positive, Inconclusive, Malicious, Suspicious and True Positive. The verdict is in the top-left region of the Incident Detail page.

quotes: Analysts and agents can set the following verdicts:
The Incident Detail page appears. The verdict is located in the top-left region of the page.
Benign: The incident is confirmed to pose no security risk or was successfully blocked inline by existing controls (e.g., ZIA inline policy block).
False Positive: The incident is determined to be a benign event or authorized activity incorrectly flagged as a security threat.
Inconclusive: The incident is unable to be assigned a definitive conclusion automatically due to insufficient telemetry or data access constraints
Malicious: The incident is a confirmed security threat requiring active remediation or containment workflows.
Suspicious: The incident is flagged with potential threat indicators requiring specialized human expertise
True Positive: The incident is a verified security event

statuses.statement: The Taking Action on Incidents page lists these statuses that analysts and AI agents can set: Discovered, Opened, Acknowledged, Not Remediated (with the reasons Testing, False Positive and Authorized Activity), Confirmed and Closed. Confirmed means the incident is closed and the assigned verdict is confirmed correct; Closed means it is closed without passing judgment on the verdict. The status is in the top-right region of the Incident Detail page.

quotes: Analysts and AI agents can set the following statuses:
The Incident Detail page appears. The status is located in the top-right region of the page.
Discovered: The incident was first identified via a series of alerts before any investigation has begun.
Opened: An analyst has begun actively investigating the incident.
Acknowledged: The incident has been reviewed and confirmed to be a legitimate issue requiring further action.
Not Remediated:
Testing: The activity was performed as part of explicit security testing, such as penetration testing.
False Positive: The incident was investigated and determined not to be a security threat.
Authorized Activity: The activity under investigation was necessary for a valid job function.
Confirmed: The incident is closed and the assigned verdict is confirmed to be correct.
Closed: The incident is closed without passing judgment on the assigned verdict.

playbook-recommendation.statement: Playbooks are typically executed when an incident requires remediation, such as when the verdict is Malicious or the status is updated to Ready to Remediate, and the Threat Response Recommendation Agent suggests playbooks in the AI Response Actions section of the incident details view. Recommendations carry labels such as Success, Proposed or Failed, and when an execution partly succeeds or fails across entities, View shows each entity's execution status.

quotes: Playbooks are typically executed when an incident requires remediation, such as when the verdict is set to Malicious or the status is updated to Ready to Remediate.
the Threat Response Recommendation Agent suggests relevant playbooks in the AI Response Actions section of the incident details view.
taking note of recommendation labels such as Success, Proposed, or Failed.
If a playbook execution succeeds partially or fails across listed entities, click View to inspect the specific execution status for each individual entity associated with the recommended action.

custom-incident.statement: A custom incident is created from one or more alerts selected on the Alerts page by clicking Create Incident; the Create Incident from Alerts drawer takes a Severity, a Status, a Title (entered, or the one Agentic SOC generates automatically) and a Verdict.

quotes: You can create a custom incident based on one or more alerts from the collated list available on the Alerts page in Agentic SOC.
Select one or more alerts from the list, then click Create Incident.
Severity: Select a severity level (e.g., High, Medium, Low) from the drop-down menu.
Status: Select a status (e.g., Discovered, Remediated, Confirmed) from the drop-down menu.
Title: Enter a title for the incident, or use the title automatically generated by Agentic SOC.
Verdict: Select a verdict (e.g., Accepted, Executed, Partial) from the drop-down menu.

custom-incident-examples.statement: The Creating a Custom Incident page gives the example statuses Discovered, Remediated and Confirmed and the example verdicts Accepted, Executed and Partial for the drawer's drop-downs, while the Taking Action on Incidents page has its own lists of verdicts and statuses that analysts and agents can set.

quotes: Status: Select a status (e.g., Discovered, Remediated, Confirmed) from the drop-down menu.
Verdict: Select a verdict (e.g., Accepted, Executed, Partial) from the drop-down menu.
Analysts and agents can set the following verdicts:
Analysts and AI agents can set the following statuses:

custom-incident-examples.conditions: Rests on an absence in the captured Taking Action page: reading its two lists in full, the verdicts are Benign, False Positive, Inconclusive, Malicious, Suspicious and True Positive (none of Accepted, Executed, Partial) and the statuses are Discovered, Opened, Acknowledged, Not Remediated, Confirmed and Closed (no status named Remediated). The page's own wording is "e.g.", so the examples do not say the drop-downs offer only those values; the comparison is of the examples against the other page's lists.

ready-to-remediate-scope.statement: The Taking Action on Incidents page names the status Ready to Remediate in its playbook paragraph, while its own list of statuses that analysts and AI agents can set does not include it.

quotes: Analysts and AI agents can set the following statuses:
the status is updated to Ready to Remediate.

ready-to-remediate-scope.conditions: Rests on an absence in the captured page: its status list (Discovered, Opened, Acknowledged, Not Remediated, Confirmed, Closed) has no Ready to Remediate entry.

status-customization.statement: Incident and alert statuses have a default set, and you can configure existing statuses (for example reorder and rename) and create new ones on the Statuses page, choosing Alert or Incident from the Entity Type drop-down menu. A new status is added within one of the existing buckets with Add Status, and when you add a bucket with Add Bucket, its Closed and Remediated options select whether the bucket automatically includes the status.

quotes: Agentic SOC provides a default set of statuses for incidents and alerts, but you can configure existing statuses (e.g., reorder and rename) and create new statuses.
The Statuses page opens. Select Alert from the Entity Type drop-down menu.
the process is the same for customizing incident statuses.
Click Add Status to add a new status within one of the existing buckets
Click Add Bucket to add a status bucket, then configure the new bucket:
Closed: (Optional) Select whether the bucket automatically includes this status.
Remediated: (Optional) Select whether the bucket automatically includes this status.

customize-detail-pages.statement: Agentic SOC provides a default view of alert and incident details that you can customize (the default configuration) or supplement by creating new configurations, selecting Incident from the Entity drop-down menu. A tab's Type is Fields, 2 Columns, Text or Table, and Save keeps the existing configuration while Save as New Type saves a new one.

quotes: select Incident from the Entity drop-down menu.
Agentic SOC provides a default view with important alert and incident details, but you can customize the default configuration or create new configurations.
Type: Select whether to display data on the tab as Fields, 2 Columns, Text, or Table.
Click Save to save the existing configuration, or click Save as New Type to save a new configuration.

status-definitions.title: What Ready to Remediate and Remediated mean, and which buckets exist by default
status-definitions.detail: The Taking Action page names Ready to Remediate and the custom-incident drawer gives Remediated as an example status, but no captured page defines either, and none names the default status buckets that the Closed and Remediated bucket options refer to.

drawer-example-values.title: How the drawer's example verdicts and statuses relate to the lists
drawer-example-values.detail: The drawer's examples (Accepted, Executed, Partial; Remediated) are not in the Taking Action page's lists, and the page words them as e.g. No captured source says which values the Create Incident from Alerts drop-downs offer.

incident-permissions.title: Which role permissions the Incidents page, statuses and UI config need
incident-permissions.detail: Only incident workflows state a permission (see soc-workbench.incident-rules); the captured pages for the Incidents page, statuses and detail-page customization name none.
